segments: The Chronography of Barhebraeus.
Baiju
began to prepare an army for himself.
And he sent one of his servants whose name was Toghrul-khapeh towards Melitene,
to organize for him an army of Kurds, Ma'addites, and Turkmens.
And when he arrived,
he went to Hisn Ziyad.
And he sent and brought from the East two Kurdish chieftains:
one, Sharaf al-Din Ahmad bar Bilas, and he gave him Melitene;
and the other, Sharaf al-Din Muhammad bar Shaykh 'Adi, and he gave him Hisn Ziyad.
And when bar Bilas arrived,
he was not accepted by the people of Melitene,
because they had sworn allegiance to Rukn al-Din.
And he began to fight against the citizens.
And they were in distress from him the whole winter;
and there was a famine,
for one qafiz of wheat rose to one hundred and twenty sultanis.
And when the people of Melitene could endure him no longer,
they rose up against this bar Bilas and killed about three hundred of his men.
And he fled and crossed over into the district of Claudia,
and set fire to the monastery of Madiq and the monastery of Mor Asya on Palm Sunday, the first of Nisan,
and wrought great devastation in that district,
and likewise in the district of Gubos.
And from there he directed his way
on the road to Amid;
and there he was overtaken by the lord of Mayyafariqin and was killed.
And that other one, the son of Shaykh 'Adi, who was in Hisn Ziyad,
after many tribulations which he had made the people of the fortress endure,
took his womenfolk (his brothers {OCR?})
and set out towards Kemakh to go to the aid of Sultan 'Izz al-Din;
and there the troops of Angurak Noyan overtook him and killed him.
Now Sultan 'Izz al-Din, when he heard of the evil end that had befallen these Kurds who had come to his aid,
sent as commander of the army to Melitene a man called 'Ali Bahadur,
a man of short stature and small size,
yet stout, warlike, and very skilled in the matters of war.
When he arrived,
the people of Melitene received him.
And from him came help to the citizens and to the district;
and the roads were opened,
and they brought wheat from every place.
